rationale: Test-only hardening of two existing pure modules in one subsystem (src/analytics). Targets: normalizer-props-execution.ts exports buildExecutionFamilyProps with an 8-arm event-type switch, each arm carrying invalid_value/unknown_enum rejection paths (parseEnum misses, nullableInt/readNullableBool absent-vs-null, byteBucket/countBucket bounds, PseudonymSchema toolNameKey branch, the pinned 300_000 timeout) — its companion suite today has a single test; intent/classifier.ts exports classifyToolTrace/classifyMetadata/classifyHybrid/toClassifierToolSlug plus three decision tables (TOOL_BY_INTENT, STRUCTURED_SIGNAL_BY_INTENT, RUNTIME_SLUGS_BY_INTENT) with abstention, >3-goal overflow, meta-tool skip, unmapped-slug conflict, and command_family fallbacks — its companion suite only pins frozen-corpus parity. New suites live in tests/analytics/ next to the existing files. cross_module=true: the work spans two independent modules, reads six shared support modules (normalizer-shared, event-props, source-facts[-execution], taxonomy, controlled-types, contracts) for fixtures/enum shapes, and touches the mutation toolchain config (baseline.json registration at measured scores; overrides.json only if coverage discovery misses the new suites). normalizer.ts and jobs/intent.ts are read-context consumers whose behavior must stay unchanged; a mutant-kill-exposed defect would be fixed in the target modules themselves and recorded in change notes. No DB, no provider interfaces, no credentials (tests derive pseudonym keys from a synthetic 32-byte buffer via createFactKeyDeriver). Novelty is existing-modules: no new top-level module, suites extend existing test files and the local bun:test patterns.
